diagnoses.label: amount_fallback_to_next_line_on_payment_tender_keyword_leak
diagnoses.general_pattern: When the keyword-matched total line's own numeric parse fails or produces a corrupted value, the extractor consults the immediately-following line and accepts its last monetary token without checking whether that fallback line is a payment/tender/change line. For receipts whose Total line is followed by Cash/Payment/Received, this routes the amount into a tender value that happens to equal the real total minus/plus change, producing a wrong but two-decimal-shaped number.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Guarded split-line fallback was invoked whenever the keyword line yielded no number, with no payment-keyword guard and no backoff to an earlier same-tier candidate.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 074.jpg prediction '702.00' then final '102.00' flipped vs oracle receipt showing 'Total Amt Rounded 102.00' and 'Payment: 102.00'; agent's own trace shows 'Total inel. of GBT 702.00' and 'Toial Amt Rounded ... 102.00' with OCR corruption; feedback flags amount_correct=false for 074 where the printed total is 102.00 but recorded prediction is '702.00'. The chosen tier-4 TOTAL candidate contained an OCR-corrupted amount and the fallback did not screen out tender/payment-shaped neighbours.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before accepting a next-line fallback value, verify the fallback line is pre-cutoff, does not match any exclusion keyword, and does not match payment/tender keywords (CASH, PAYMENT, TENDERED, RECEIVED, CHANGE, VISA, MASTERCARD, CARD, CREDIT, DEBIT); if the original keyword line contains digits that failed numeric parsing, treat it as OCR corruption and back off to the previous same-tier candidate instead of consulting the next line.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Keep the guarded split-line fallback only for keyword lines containing zero digits; otherwise iterate same-tier candidates from last to first until one yields a parseable monetary token, and screen any fallback line against both exclusion and payment-tender keyword sets before use.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to receipt-OCR tasks that declare a priority-tier keyword list and an exclusion list, and whose total value may be printed on the same line as the keyword; does not apply when the task contract explicitly directs reading the next-line value regardless of keyword-line digits.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Non-receipt OCR tasks, free-form document extraction, or any task where payment/tender tokens are themselves the target field.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Mechanism anchor: receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation (step 4 Guarded split-line fallback)

diagnoses.label: amount_truncation_from_ocr_digit_dropout_not_cross_checked
diagnoses.general_pattern: When Tesseract silently truncates a trailing digit inside a monetary token (e.g. '88.17' read as '88.1' or '23.26' read as '23.2x'), the extractor accepts the first parseable two-decimal (or one-decimal) number on a tier-matching line without cross-checking against other corroborating anchors (payment total, cash-change arithmetic, prior same-tier candidate). A one-decimal match is also silently padded or an earlier same-tier candidate is ignored.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Monetary regex accepts the last token on the chosen line as authoritative; no corroboration pass over Payment/Cash/Visa/Change lines or prior same-tier candidates; no rejection of one-decimal matches.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 064.jpg predicted '88.17' is correct but historical trace shows a 88.10 variant produced when 'Total Gross C RM 88.1' was selected under TOTAL RM tier; 077.jpg predicted '23.26' flagged amount_correct=false, where the receipt image shows 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' and a later 'TOTAL: 23.25' after rounding adj -0.01 - the chosen candidate did not reconcile against the rounded TOTAL anchor; 074.jpg analogous truncation pattern. Agent's own think trace documents awareness that 88.17 vs 88.10 depends on which same-tier line is picked but no cross-check was added.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: After selecting a tier candidate, (a) reject one-decimal matches in favour of other same-tier two-decimal candidates; (b) corroborate against other total-adjacent anchors in the same OCR variant (Payment, Cash, Cash − Change, matching Subtotal + Tax ± Rounding); (c) prefer the candidate agreeing with at least one non-tier anchor over an outlier that differs by a trailing-digit substitution; (d) when two same-tier candidates disagree, prefer the one whose value matches the explicitly rounded line.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Apply the monetary_two_decimal_invariant strictly (reject one-decimal), and run a bounded corroboration pass over same-receipt non-tier anchors before writing the amount.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt-style tasks where totals are printed with exactly two fractional digits and multiple corroborating lines (Payment, Cash, Change, Subtotal+Tax) are typically present. Does not apply to tasks where single-decimal or integer totals are legitimate.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Free-form numeric extraction without a declared two-decimal invariant; invoice IDs; phone numbers; quantities.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Mechanism anchors monetary_two_decimal_invariant and ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck and multi_variant_consensus_over_tier_priority

diagnoses.label: null_vs_empty_string_writeback_violation_for_amount
diagnoses.general_pattern: When amount extraction fails, the writeback writes an empty string ("") into the cell instead of a true null. For task contracts that declare failed extractions as null, this produces a value-mismatch at verifier time even when the schema and row ordering are correct.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Extractor returns "" (empty string) on failure, or routes None through f-string/str() before cell assignment; verifier reads a non-null empty string where None is required.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 078.jpg prediction row shows total_amount='' (empty string) while date is populated; feedback flags amount_correct=false for 078. The receipt image clearly shows 'Grand Total : 92.80' as the final total, so this is a writeback-contract failure, not a pure OCR failure (the agent's own trace earlier extracted 92.80 for 078). The final delivered xlsx preserved empty string rather than None, causing the amount field to be scored wrong.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: On extraction failure the function must return Python None, and openpyxl/pandas assignment must receive None directly (no f-string, no str()). On delivery, reload workbook and assert `cell.value is None` for every failed-extraction cell, not `cell.value == ''`.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Preserve a strict null-vs-empty-string contract end-to-end: None in extraction return, None in cell assignment, and a reload-time assertion that failed cells satisfy `cell.value is None`.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to tasks whose contract explicitly distinguishes null from empty string in output cells (declared here by the task prompt: 'If extraction fails for either field, the value is set to null'). Does not apply where '' is an acceptable sentinel or a placeholder string is required.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Financial models with formulas, templates where empty strings are the convention, or tasks silent on null handling.
diagnoses.target_section: Preserving null vs empty string on writeback + Delivery contract verification for data-only xlsx outputs

diagnoses.label: iteration_budget_exhausted_without_batch_diagnostic_consolidation
diagnoses.general_pattern: Agent runs an iteration-per-image interactive debug loop rather than a single consolidated diagnostic pass over the full batch followed by a small set of pattern/variant edits and one re-run. Iteration limit is reached (termination_reason=max_iterations at 65 iterations) with amount accuracy still below 90%, meaning several addressable OCR-amount errors remain unfixed despite being observable from aggregated per-image traces.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Sequential per-receipt debugging consumes iteration budget; no single dump of per-variant OCR slices, candidate (tier, value, anchor) lists, and current predictions across all N images; no batch-wise consolidated edit.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Execution metadata: agent_iterations=65, max_iterations_at_source=65, termination_reason='max_iterations', iteration_limit_reached=true. Response tool-call counts: terminal 27, think 22, file_editor 16, no invoke_skill. Three amount errors (074, 077, 078) remain at termination; the trajectory shows repeated single-image reasoning blocks instead of a consolidated diagnostic.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Run one diagnostic sweep that, per image, dumps the per-variant OCR slice around keywords, the candidate (tier, value, anchor_type) list, and the current prediction; then plan a small consolidated edit set (regex + variant + fallback-guard) covering several failures together and re-run once; avoid interactive per-image debug loops.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Follow the batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit workflow note: aggregate failures, consolidate pattern edits, re-run once.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to batch OCR extraction tasks over N≥~10 images where iteration budget is bounded. Does not apply to single-image or interactive-exploration tasks.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Single-document OCR, interactive QA, or tasks where per-item branching is required by the contract.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Workflow note: batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit

diagnoses.label: date_locale_ambiguity_on_dd_mm_vs_mm_dd
diagnoses.general_pattern: When a receipt date is printed with both components ≤12 (e.g. 09/08/2018 interpretable as DD/MM or MM/DD), the extractor applies a fixed ordering without consulting a declared locale or a batch-dominant ordering inferred from unambiguous rows in the same batch.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Date regex is applied with a single hard-coded component order; no locale declaration check; no batch-majority inference from rows where day>12.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 034.jpg predicted date '2018-08-09' flagged date_correct=false; receipt image clearly shows 'Date: 09/03/2018' (DD/MM/YYYY, Malaysian locale) for GOGIANT ENGINEERING / PERNIAGAAN ZHENG HUI, which should yield 2018-03-09 — not 2018-08-09. The agent parsed '09/08/2018' from an unrelated line or inverted the day/month ordering. All other dates in the batch where day>12 (23/01/2019, 29/12/2017, 15/06/2017, 18/03/18, 23/03/2018, 25/02/18, 21/02/18, 20-02-18, 19/02/2018, 20/3/2018, 29-10-2017, 21/09/2017, 30/05/2017, 13/03/2017, 12/01/18) unambiguously fix DD/MM/YYYY as the dominant ordering, so the batch-majority rule would have caught 034.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Bind the extracted date to a label (prefer DATE-labelled lines, not Print/Closed/Loyalty), parse under declared locale (DD/MM/YYYY for Malaysian receipts), and when ambiguous consult the batch-dominant ordering inferred from unambiguous rows (any first component >12 fixes DD/MM/YYYY).
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Apply receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale with locale=DD/MM/YYYY and a batch-majority tiebreaker before emitting ISO 8601.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt-style tasks with locale-dependent numeric date formats and a batch of related receipts. Does not apply to tasks that supply explicit date-ordering metadata per record or that use month-name formats.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: ISO-already-formatted dates; locale-agnostic timestamps; non-receipt documents.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Mechanism anchor: receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale

overlay.composition_issue: The receipt overlay already defines the right mechanism anchors (keyword-tier disambiguation, two-decimal invariant, ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck, multi_variant_consensus_over_tier_priority, null_vs_empty_string_contract, batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit) but the current run shows the agent did not route through them: amount errors on 074 and 077 are same-line/same-tier disambiguation failures that step 4 (payment/tender guarded fallback) and the arithmetic cross-check anchor already address; the 078 '' writeback contradicts the null_vs_empty_string_contract already present in both image-ocr and xlsx; the 034 date error is exactly the DD/MM vs MM/DD locale case the receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale anchor already covers; and iteration budget was exhausted despite the batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit workflow note. The gap is strength and salience of these anchors (particularly step 4 guard and the writeback contract), not missing mechanisms.
preservation_constraints: Keep the scope boundary that confines the receipt overlay to tasks declaring their own keyword priority / exclusion / null conventions; do not fold receipt-specific hints into openai-vision, pdf, video-frame-extraction, or generic xlsx guidance.
Preserve the negative boundary against fabricating values and against hard-coding expected outputs from any particular task.
Preserve the two-decimal invariant and the explicit rejection of one-decimal padding.
Preserve the null_vs_empty_string_contract scope: only apply when the task contract declares null as the failure sentinel; do not generalize to tasks where '' is acceptable.
Preserve the batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit workflow note's scope (batch OCR over N images with bounded iteration budget).
Do not add any task-specific keyword tables (e.g. the exact 22-image answer set); keep anchors reusable.

package_assessment.rationale: All four scored failures (074 amount, 077 amount, 078 amount, 034 date) are observable from the receipt images and OCR traces and map cleanly onto existing receipt-overlay mechanism anchors already present in the current candidate SKILL.md set (keyword-priority disambiguation with payment-tender guarded fallback; two-decimal invariant plus arithmetic cross-check and multi-variant consensus; null_vs_empty_string_contract plus xlsx delivery self-check; receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale with batch-majority tiebreaker). The infrastructure signals (max_iterations termination, 0 skill invocations, 0 model calls by preprocessor) indicate the mechanisms exist but were not followed strongly enough — i.e. a skill-strengthening problem, not an infrastructure/executor-only failure. No hidden gold defects or oracle values were used; diagnosis rests entirely on the delivered xlsx rows, the field-level feedback flags, the 22 source receipt images, and the agent's own trajectory analysis.
